messages.subject: R-Ring
parts:
Before I got to looking at R-Shiny (Which is lovely) I explored a lot of different tech.

One of these was clojure-ring/noir/compojure, which has analogues in other languages.

Requests to the server are in the form server:/a/b/c or similar, where a/b/c/ can be names of services, or arguments to the service.

The service is rest-ful which usually means there is no server-carried state (that matters).

This also supports XHR (XML Http Request) so JS can ask for more (or more detailed) data.

Is there any support for such a thing in R?  My d3 application is increasingly drifting away from how I understand the Shiny use-case, in the following ways:

  * a single javascript component makes request for a different record, or more detail from the current record
  * URL should reflect the current view, either using a PATH or ? or # component
  * reactives in the current sense do too much work, since they are based on push from inputs, not pull from outputs

It would be great if I could understand the problem in terms of the current shiny implementation (anyone?), but otherwise I will start looking for a ring-type solution on R.

-Alex Brown

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: R-Ring
parts:
Hi Alex, thanks for the feedback!

It's early days for Shiny, we're just laying the foundation right now. You're at the ragged edge of what Shiny is capable of today, but what you're trying to do is directly in our crosshairs.

If all you want is what ring/noir/compojure provide, you should take a look at Jeffrey Horner's Rook package plus rApache.
> a single javascript component makes request for a different record, or more detail from the current record

This will be a central scenario for Shiny moving forward. For the current version of Shiny I didn't want to go too far down this road until we had adequate user feedback for the simpler stuff. The main challenge for Shiny, as I see it, is to see whether the reactive-programming paradigm can work at least as well as imperative programming when the lines between input and output start to blur. So far I think we have reason to be fairly optimistic :)
> URL should reflect the current view

This is out of scope for Shiny for now. We do want to enable bookmarking/sharing via URL but it's not at all clear that we'll end up with pretty URLs like the ones you're talking about, as they need to capture all the input state which might be arbitrarily complicated (nested data structures, large amounts of data, etc.).
> reactives in the current sense do too much work, since they are based on push from inputs, not pull from outputs

We're working on this right now. You can try a prototype:

install.packages("devtools")
devtools::install_github("shiny", "rstudio", branch="jcheng/lazy-reactive-functions")

which is one easy fix (not guaranteed to be the final one though). We're also working on having non-visible outputs not do work. It's really important to us to get this right!
